featured.reason: Compiler changes directly affect Rust development
featured.suggestedSummary: A new proposal for per-package-target feature unification aims to improve the Rust development experience, particularly for embedded workspaces. This change would allow developers to specify features at the package level, tailored to specific targets, enhancing flexibility and organization. If implemented, this could streamline configurations and reduce complexity in multi-target projects, making Rust more efficient for embedded systems and cross-platform applications.

featured.title: Pqrascv-core: Post-quantum (ML-DSA-65) remote attestation with built-in SLSA provenance for no_std embedded Rust
featured.summary:
Even if large-scale quantum systems are still years away, long-lived trust systems like firmware signing and infrastructure identity are already exposed to “store now, break later” attacks.
Still early days for the project, but I’m trying to push it toward something actually deployable, not just theoretical.
featured.reason: Post-quantum security is crucial for Rust developers
featured.suggestedTitle: PQ-RASCV: Post-Quantum Security for Embedded Rust
featured.suggestedSummary: The PQ-RASCV-core project introduces post-quantum (ML-DSA-65) remote attestation with built-in SLSA provenance for no_std embedded Rust environments. This initiative addresses the 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat by incorporating quantum-resistant algorithms, crucial for long-term security in embedded systems. By integrating with the Embassy framework, this project enhances Rust's capabilities in building secure, future-proof embedded applications.

quickNews.title: Idea for a buffered channel
quickNews.summary:
paddor:
have you considered zstd
I am using MS_SQL COMPRESS, I don't think anything as advanced as zstd will be available for a long time! It is plenty fast enough, these are old emails (and other documents) that are rarely accessed and the load is low. This is a database that goes back about 25 years. I managed (through a variety of compression techniques) to reduce it by a factor of about 5.
